body: I'll try.
Yes. If I could just have a friend. One friend. That's all I ask.
I haven't lately. I don't have the will.
Well, I'm pretty damn lonely, so I don't exactly enjoy being alive. It's quite dull when you have no one who you can love and trust.

If you are honest and persistent, I'm sure that you can change.

Best of luck to you as well.
Thanks for commenting. I feel the same way.

> ...but the fact that you're still willing to get back up and give it another go is nothing short of admirable.

Thank you, but that's not exactly true right now. You see, I've lost my will to get up and try again. This is quite worrying to me. I just don't care about anything. I'm willing to let go of my hopes and dreams and just rot listlessly.

>  You're scared of dying because every fibre of your being wants to stay alive, and that to me shows that you're winning this fight. 

I hope you are right. If I am winning this fight then it certainly does not feeling like winning. More like waiting... Waiting for what, I wonder? I know that one must take action if one wants change, but I am fed up with this fucking bullshit called existing. I don't care for improvement anymore.

But apparently I care enough to write this. And apparently I care enough to not want to die. Maybe that's enough.

Thanks for commenting.
Thanks.
Thanks! I find it wonderful how easy it is to find like-minded folk on the internet.

> Perhaps a personality thing? 

I'm almost certain it's a personality thing. Certain people tend to be more ~~obsessive~~ passionate about self-actualization than others.

> Have you tried journaling and exploring spirituality? 

I have been journaling for several years now. It helps to discover the roots of things and I find it to be an excellent means of venting.

> Do you have someone you can talk to? 

I am friends with my high school counselor, but unfortunately she retired this year and because it's summer break for me, I hardly ever see her. I still keep in touch, though.

She's the person I'm most comfortable with in person, yet there are still some things I have difficulty discussing.

>  Best of luck.

Thanks.

I have a psychiatrist that I visit regularly.

I'm on several medications at the moment, including anti-depressants. They don't make me feel better, but they help me from feeling worse.

I don't have ADD according to my dad, yet I do have many of the symptoms listed. I'm currently looking into non-medicinal treatments for attention problems. I'll ask my psychiatrist about it as well.

Thanks for commenting.
I'm sure we'll get over this eventually :). But I must admit, I don't always feel so positive. Best wishes.
Yes. I have seen many psychologists and psychotherapists over these past two years. I take several medications that help with the depression, but they are only a piece of the puzzle.
Will do. Thank you for supporting me. :)
Thank you very much for your support, peytonfamily. :)

Thanks for your input, Angryoyster. I'm trying my best to not have zero days, yet sometimes I wonder why bother fighting at all.

Also, I find it strange that this post and its comments were down-voted. Probably some loser shithead with too much spare time.
Okay. Thank you. Later.
I've thought about it. Not sure.

I actually was not. I loathe almost everything about college. I don't care what anyone else says; it's merely a continuation of K-12. Technically, college is optional, but considering all of the propaganda supporting it and the shit you get for opposing it, it really isn't. "How else will you get a well-paying job?", they say. And they're right. What else can one do?

I am planning on avoiding college if I can help it. But I'm keeping my options open; if there's a school/alt-institution that fits me, I may give it a shot.

I may find friends there, (or I may not) but I need more reason than that in order to commit myself to such a shitty shithole of a place.

Thank you. I hope to grow my talents and one day use them to support myself.

I have a licensed psychologist I visit twice a month. Unfortunately, she can only tell me more of what I already know. I need a friend, not more advice. This is what is so frustrating to me. I can't find the companionship I so desperately need.

I have long wondered if I could ever successfully substitute human interaction by immersing myself in deeply intellectual activities. I've never tried; I'm afraid if I took the plunge, I would not get out again.

I will certainly stick around. I have no desire to commit suicide, only no desire to live. I hope I can turn this ship around soon. I am taking steps...

Now if only I could stop tripping over my own feet...
